verify_findings.what: Named files are measured outside the gate's own default measured set. `make validate-changed` passes changed docs paths to these positional gates. So an edit to docs/inbox.md (the trap inbox) or to docs/README.md's hand-written rows, on a branch that does not also change the structure file, turns kb-shape red with KB-001/KB-002 findings that `make validate` never gives. The driver's repro line `make gate G=check-kb-shape` (no files) then passes, so the red cannot be reproduced from it. The same gap lets docs-style measure a named stamped hub, against page-shape-C7 ('a stamped hub … never measured'), and measure README/inbox only when named. The reverse also holds: a page outside the kind folders with no structure row gets no KB-001 in the whole run.

frontmatter-C4 (description one line, ≤160 characters) is not held for pages the structure file does not publish. The frontmatter gate leaves length and the block-scalar check to PAGE-005. docs-style's whole run measures only published rows, so docs/inbox.md, docs/README.md and any unlisted page pass with any description. frontmatter-C1/C4 cover every page, published or not.

The lane made extract-model read the frontmatter of docs/reference/*.md and docs/concepts/*.md (title → row label, level, tags → hub). The model-fresh row's `scans` did not gain those globs, so `make validate-changed` after editing a reference page's title runs neither model-fresh nor map-fresh and stays green while the structure file is stale. This is the class of bug 4a0658a fixed for the lane's own gates. Likewise docs-style's scans omit site/src/content/docs/**/*.mdx, which its measured set includes.

The map gate reads links with outsideFences only. HTML comments and inline code spans are not blanked, as check-repo-links.ts's blankInline blanks them, so the repo has two readings of the one link-reading convention. A commented-out map row still counts as mapping its page, which is invisible on the rendered map (docs-map-C1 passes when it should fail). A code-span sample link on the map is reported as a dead row.

frontmatter-C1 asks that each required key be non-empty, but `tags: []` passes the frontmatter gate. Nothing on this branch reports an empty tag list: the count belongs to the other lane's tags gate. Six published reference and concept pages and the inbox also carry one tag, below page-block's 2–5, and nothing on this branch reports it.

frontmatter-C8: the exercise regime checks that `tags` is present but not that it is an inline list. An exercise writing `tags:` as a block list gets no 'not inline, every tag dropped' finding, although the page regime and the frontmatter behaviours give one. A one-tag exercise also passes; the 3–5 count is tags-C2's.

A fence opens at any indentation, so a four-space-indented ``` line (indented code under page-shape-C3, not a fence) opens a 'fence' that never closes. Every later line is hidden from every rule and from the H1 rule (page-shape-C2/C3).

Two false findings against link-integrity-C1/C3. Emphasis underscores are kept in heading slugs, so `## Use _this_ one` offers `use-_this_-one` where GitHub gives `use-this-one`. Indented code blocks are not blanked, so a link sample in one is read as a link, although code holds no links.

page-shape-C1 says the shape gate's findings are never in the `[name] FAIL` shape. With the structure file (or content model) missing, docs-style and kb-shape print `[docs-style] FAIL …`. The triage 'Page shape' section does not list this finding.

The KB-013 row says `aliases` is an inline list, `[]` when the page has none. The gate accepts a missing key, and 79 kind pages omit it (5 write `[]`). Rule and tree disagree, and rule-identity says the disagreeing side gets fixed.

These files are outside the lane's ownership: the harness lane owns the 46 skills and their route gate. The harness lane made the same `../../` → `../../../` fix (e36ba5f) and also reshaped both files (9a91254), so the two branches change the same lines at different positions: a likely merge conflict, though harmless to resolve.

Named files widen the measured set instead of narrowing it. A named page-regime file that is neither a structure row nor in a kind folder is measured anyway, so the gate fails on a clean tree for docs/inbox.md and docs/README.md, which by design have no row. Because the kb-shape row scans docs/**/*.md with positional: true, `make validate-changed` goes red for any change that touches only the trap inbox or the map. The printed repro, `make gate G=check-kb-shape`, then passes.

The page list comes from `git ls-files --cached` with no check that each file is still on disk. When a tracked page is deleted or moved with plain rm or mv and not yet staged, the batched parser call throws, and the gate exits 2 (misuse) on a valid invocation. That run checks no frontmatter at all. docs-map, repo-links, kb-shape and docs-style all filter by existsSync; this gate alone does not. The planned move of the concept pages into docs/reference/ is exactly this situation.

The map gate treats text inside an inline code span or an HTML comment on the map, or on a hub, as a link that maps the page. The repo-links gate in the same lane reads neither as a link. So commenting out a map row hides the page while docs-map stays green. A commented-out row pointing at a deleted page also gives a false 'does not exist' finding. docs-map-C1 is about links a reader can follow.

verify_findings.where: tools/src/gates/check-docs-style.ts measuredSet/publishedSources plus the named path `named.filter(shaped)`; check-doc-frontmatter.ts (leaves length to PAGE-005)
verify_findings.what: frontmatter-C4 and PAGE-005 (one plain line of at most 160 characters) are never checked on docs/README.md or docs/inbox.md in the whole run. The frontmatter gate leaves length and block-scalar checks to PAGE-005, but docs-style's default set holds only pages the structure file publishes. Yet naming such a page measures it, so `make validate` passes and `make validate-changed` fails on the same tree.

Inline code is exempt from PAGE-006, but a code span opened by two backticks is not recognised. The single-backtick regex removes the empty pairs and leaves the URL behind, so the gate reports a false PAGE-006.

PAGE-008 and page-shape-C5 say the Next steps section is one sentence, then the list, then nothing. The gate only flags a section that opens with its list or has prose after it, so two prose paragraphs before the list pass. The kit has the same gap.

Two readings differ from CommonMark. (1) A fence may open at any indentation, so a top-level line of four spaces then ``` opens a fence that never closes. page-shape-C3 says a line indented four spaces is code. Every later line becomes invisible to every rule. (2) The H4 pattern needs no space after the hashes, so `####word`, which is not a heading, is reported as PAGE-002. The H1 and H2 patterns do require the space.

A link is judged present by fs.existsSync, which ignores case on macOS. A link with the wrong case passes locally but fails on the ubuntu-latest CI runner (.github/workflows/validate.yml:29). Local `make validate` is green and CI is red for the same tree.

verify_findings.where: tools/src/gates/check-repo-links.ts headingText/slugOf (keeps `_`) and anchorSet (ATX headings only)
verify_findings.what: link-integrity-C3 says a slug is the heading lower-cased with punctuation dropped. slugOf keeps `_`, so `## Using _this_ page` gives `using-_this_-page`; the spec rule, and GitHub, give `using-this-page`, so the correct link is reported dead. Setext headings offer no slug at all. That is a declared deviation, 'the dialect writes only ATX', but this gate reads all 490 repository markdown files, not only dialect pages.

verify_findings.where: tools/src/gates/check-kb-shape.ts KB-002 (bySlug, first in sort order wins)
verify_findings.what: When two pages share a slug, the finding lands on whichever path sorts first, not on the new or unlisted page. A stray copy under docs/hazards/ makes the gate blame the established, published pattern page.
